content.title: Michigan smashes Arizona in Final Four, will play UConn in title game
content.text: Updated April 4, 2026, 11:38 p.m. ETMany thought it would be the game of the tournament, but it turned into a rout for Michigan basketball.The 1-seed Wolverines beat the 1-seed Arizona Wildcats 91-73 in the national semifinal of the 2026 NCAA Tournament on Saturday, April 4, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. With the win, the Wolverines will play 2-seed UConn for the national championship on Monday, April 6.Michigan had arguably its most impressive performance of the year against the title-contending Wildcats, holding a lead throughout the game and handing Arizona its worst loss of the season. The Wolverines put up an exemplary offensive performance, becoming the first team in tournament history to score at least 90 points in five tournament games, and mostly with their leading scorer nursing a knee injury.Watch the Final Four on Sling TVWolverines big man Yaxel Lendeborg left the game midway through the first half with an MCL sprain and ankle injury on his left leg, but returned to start the second half. Though he finished the game with double figures in scoring, his injury will remain a question as the Wolverines prepare for Monday's game against the Huskies.Michigan is looking for its second national title, with only a banner from 1989 hanging from the Crisler Center rafters. Meanwhile, UConn and coach Dan Hurley are looking for their third national title in four seasons after the Huskies won back-to-back titles in 2023 and 2024. Here's how it all went down. Michigan wins, advances to national title gameFINAL: Michigan 91, Arizona 73.Michigan took a 10-3 lead and never looked back, leading the game from tip to tail and spanking the 1-seed Wildcats.The Wolverines will play 2-seed UConn on Monday, April 6, with the national title on the line. Michigan makes history2H, 2:24: Michigan 90, Arizona 70.Michigan basketball has made history tonight, becoming the first team in NCAA history to score at least 90 points in five tournament games.Another record falls in Michigan's quest for a national title. Five Wolverines in double figures2H, 4:42: Michigan 86, Arizona 64.Even with the first-team All-American Yaxel Lendeborg on the bench for most of the game, Michigan has put on an offensive showcase tonight with five players in double-figures in scoring.C Aday Mara (26 points).G Trey McKenney (16).F Lendeborg (11).PG Elliot Cadeau (11).F Morez Johnson Jr. (10).Arizona, meanwhile, has only three players in double figures, with forward Koa Peat leading the Wildcats with 14 points. Michigan cruising in second half2H, 7:33: Michigan 81, Arizona 60.It's time to start making plans for Monday's national championship game.Michigan is on track to reach 100 points this game, and barring a miraculous comeback from Arizona, the Wolverines will be playing for a national championship on Monday.Also, check out this dunk from Roddy Gayle Jr. Michigan lands 5-star recruitApparently, it's always recruiting season – even in the middle of the Final Four.Five-star recruit Brandon McCoy from California's Sierra Canyon committed to Michigan for next season on the Fab Five broadcast. Trey McKenney heats up, Aday Mara slams2H, 12:17: Michigan 72, Arizona 45.Back-to-back 3-pointers from Michigan guard Trey McKenney helped Michigan keep its 20-point lead. The freshman then hit a step-back, midrange jumper to bring his total to 13, though center Aday Mara still leads all players with 19 points.He also provided the dunk of the game, a two-handed jam that rocked the entire dome. Yaxel Lendeborg hits two 3-pointers2H, 16:08: Michigan 56, Arizona 37.Michigan has eight points so far this half, and six of them have come from 3-pointers from Lendeborg, the second one giving the Wolverines a 56-36 lead.Lendeborg now has 11 points on the game, though he doesn't seem to be moving as fluidly as he did before the injury. Yaxel Lendeborg back for the second half, has MCL sprainMichigan big man Yaxel Lendeborg, who missed most of the first half after suffering an ankle injury, is back out to start the second half for the Wolverines.Per TBS's Tracy Wolfson, Lendeborg is dealing with an MCL sprain on his left knee and an ankle injury on the same side. Michigan up big at the halfEnd 1H: Michigan 48, Arizona 32.Arizona didn't lead at any point through the first half as the Wolverines open up a 16-point lead against the Wildcats.But Michigan may be missing big man Yaxel Lendeborg, who hurt his ankle in the first half and may not return in the second. Aday Mara taking control1H, 1:25: Michigan 48, Arizona 30.Michigan center Aday Mara looks unstoppable right now.With 15 points and five rebounds (both team highs), Mara has been the most impactful offensive player on both sides of the ball. The only thing that has stopped him so far is foul trouble, as he has had many spells on the bench with two personal fouls on his record. Yaxel Lendeborg heads back to locker roomAccording to TBS sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson, Lendeborg injured the same ankle that he hurt in the Big Ten tournament and is receiving treatment in the locker room. Michigan will re-evaluate his condition to see if he can return to play. Michigan extends lead1H, 4:50: Michigan 35, Arizona 23.Michigan guard Roddy Gayle Jr. ended Arizona's 9-0 run in style with a two-handed dunk over Wildcats center Motiejus Krivas. But on the other end, Krivas drew a foul from Michigan big man Morez Johnson Jr.Johnson, Yaxel Lendeborg and Aday Mara all have two fouls early on for the Wolverines, putting all three bigs in foul trouble. Though Arizona point guard Jaden Bradley went to the bench with his third foul of the game, as the referees have been active so far in the half.Lendeborg was seen walking back to the bench with a towel over his head, though he didn't look like he was walking comfortably. He went back to the locker room soon after. Arizona on 7-0 run1H, 7:21: Michigan 28, Arizona 21.With Michigan big man Yaxel Lendeborg getting his injured ankle looked at in the locker room, Arizona went on a 7-0 run to cut its deficit to seven points. Wildcats forward Koa Peat leads the team with six points. Yaxel Lendeborg appears hurt1H, 8:51: Michigan 28, Arizona 14Michigan big man Yaxel Lendeborg appeared to hurt his ankle as he landed while fouled on a layup attempt. After taking a minute to collect himself, he hit both free throws before being subbed out and headed to the locker room. We await updates on his injury status.According to TBS sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson, the team expects him to be back in the game after getting some ice on his ankle. TBS also reports that Michigan trainers are checking on Lendeborg's knee as well as his ankle. Yaxel Lendeborg back in the game1H, 11:34: Michigan 22, Arizona 10.Michigan big man Yaxel Lendeborg, back in the game after recording two personal fouls, hit a corner 3-pointer for his first points of the game to make the score 22-10. According to the broadcast, the 12-point deficit midway through the first half is the largest deficit the Wildcats have faced all season. Michigan up by 111H, 14:27: Michigan 16, Arizona 5.It took about five minutes of game time for the Wolverines to build a double-digit lead.Center Aday Mara leads all scorers with six points and two rebounds, while freshman Trey McKenney got into the action with a transition dunk that led to an Arizona timeout. Yaxel Lendeborg to the bench with two early fouls1H, 15:59: Michigan 10, Arizona 3.A second-chance basket from Michigan center Aday Mara began the scoring as the Wolverines took a 2-0 lead on the first possession of the game. Arizona got Michigan big man Yaxel Lendeborg to pick up two personal fouls on the same possession, however, bringing the Michigan star to the bench.But the Wolverines offense seems to be working just fine without him. Michigan guard Nimari Burnett's 3-pointer brought Michigan's lead to 5-1 within the first two minutes of the half, while point guard Elliot Cadeau's midrange runner made it 7-1. An and-one layup (and subsequent made free-throw) from big man Morez Johnson Jr. made it 10-1 Wolverines as the Michigan defense held the Wildcats to zero field goals for nearly four minutes. Michigan starting fiveNo surprises for Michigan's starting five ahead of its game against Arizona.Arizona starting five Michigan fans gather in Ann ArborBars and gathering spots in Ann Arbor are filled with Michigan students and fans for tonight's Final Four matchup. You can check out our coverage here. The Chainsmokers performThe "bridge" performance by The Chainsmokers has completed, and we are about 17 minutes away from tipoff. Michigan taking the courtThe court is clear of Huskies and Illini as the Michigan and Arizona basketball teams warm up. Game tipoff pushed backAccording to the countdown clock on the television broadcast, the Michigan-Arizona game will tip off at 9:19 p.m. ET. UConn wins, advances to national championship gameThe 2-seed UConn Huskies beat 3-seed Illinois 71-62 in the first of two Final Four matchups tonight. They advance to the national championship game on Monday and will play the winner of the Michigan-Arizona game, which is set to tip off soon.But first, The Chainsmokers will perform at Lucas Oil Stadium before the second Final Four game tips off. Wolverines in the houseMichigan basketball has arrived to Lucas Oil Stadium ahead of its Final Four game with Arizona. The game is scheduled to tip off at approximately 8:49 p.m. ET, following the end of the national semifinal matchup between 2-seed UConn and 3-seed Illinois. Michigan availability reportNo surprises with today's availability report, with two Michigan players listed as out with injuries.Michigan: G L.J. Cason (out), F Winters Grady (out).Arizona: None. UConn up at the halfTwo-seed UConn stormed back from behind to take an 8-point lead entering the half and has a 37-29 halftime lead over 3-seed Illinois. The winner of this game will face the winner of Michigan-Arizona in Monday's national title game. Dusty May in the houseMichigan coach Dusty May was seen courtside during the first half of the Final Four matchup between 2-seed UConn and 3-seed Illinois, likely scouting the competition for Monday's national championship game (should Michigan advance, of course).What time is Michigan vs Arizona in Final Four of March Madness?Time: Approximately 8:49 p.m. ET.Date: Saturday, April 4.Location: Lucas Oil Stadium, Indianapolis.What channel is Michigan vs Arizona channel in Final Four of March Madness?Channel: TBS, TNT.Tipoff: Approximately 8:49 p.m. ET.Streaming: Sling TV, HBO Max.Audio: Westwood One Sports.Saturday's Final Four matchup between Michigan and Arizona can be watched on TBS, TNT, with streaming available on Sling TV.Watch Michigan-Arizona on Sling TVHow to watch Fab Five simulcast for Michigan vs ArizonaThe most famous team in program history will be on TV as the 2026 Wolverines try to make history of their own. Fab Five members Jalen Rose, Chris Webber, Juwan Howard, Jimmy King and Ray Jackson are set to reunite for a special alternate presentation of the Michigan vs. Arizona Final Four game on Saturday, April 4.It'll air on truTV as the traditional broadcast airs on TNT and TBS.Find more information here:How to buy Michigan vs Arizona Final Four ticketsLooking for some last minute tickets?If you've got your heart set on a trip to Lucas Oil Stadium for the game, you'll be able to get in, but it'll cost you.Tickets to get in the building cost well over $400, but the good news is that'll get you into both the Illinois-UConn game and the Michigan-Arizona one.Seats that aren't in the upper deck cost are mostly over $1,000 per ticket.Buy Michigan Final Four tickets at Lucas Oil StadiumMichigan vs Arizona predictionTony Garcia, Detroit Free Press: Michigan has felt all year if it plays its "A" game, it can beat anyone in the country. Arizona will certainly put that to the test. But this Michigan team, led by Yaxel Lendeborg (who had his best month of the season), is on a mission. The pick: U-M 86, Arizona 83.Michigan vs Arizona odds in Final FourSpread: Michigan by 1½ points.Over/under: 157½ points.Moneyline: Arizona (-102), Michigan (-118).Odds are courtesy of BetMGM as of Thursday afternoon.How many Final Fours has Michigan basketball made?Saturday will mark the Wolverines' ninth appearance in the Final Four.Here's a list of all of them:*National title win.1964196519761989*19921993201320182026Read about how they fared in those appearances below:Michigan NCAA Tournament scoresFirst round: W, 101-80 vs 16-seed Howard.Second round: W, 95-72 vs 9-seed Saint Louis.Sweet 16: W, 90-77 vs 4-seed Alabama.Elite Eight: W, 95-62 vs 6-seed Tennessee.Final Four, April 4: vs 1-seed Arizona, 8:49 p.m. ET (TBS).Championship, April 6: TBD.Need to catch up on the news during your lunch break?
